name: Pan-Seared Lemon Dill Salmon
pitch: Simple, elegant, and on the table in under 20 minutes — the lemon and dill are a classic pair that make salmon taste like a restaurant meal.
steps: Pat your salmon fillets dry with a paper towel and season generously with salt and pepper on both sides.
Heat a splash of oil in a skillet over medium-high heat until it shimmers, then lay the salmon in skin-side up.
Cook for about 4 minutes, flip, then add a knob of butter, a few sprigs of fresh dill, and squeeze half the lemon over the top.
Baste the salmon with the buttery pan juices for another 3–4 minutes until cooked through, then serve with lemon wedges.
toolSuggestion: A good non-stick or cast iron skillet

name: Garlic Dill Salmon with Pasta
pitch: Tossing flaked salmon through garlicky buttered pasta with lemon zest turns three humble ingredients into a surprisingly satisfying weeknight bowl.
steps: Boil salted water and cook whatever pasta you have on hand until al dente, reserving a cup of pasta water before draining.
Meanwhile, season the salmon with salt, pepper, and a little dill, then pan-fry in oil over medium heat for 4–5 minutes per side, then flake it into big chunks.
In the same pan, sauté a few cloves of sliced garlic in butter for 1–2 minutes, then add the drained pasta and a splash of pasta water to loosen.
Toss in the flaked salmon, a squeeze of lemon, the zest of half a lemon, and the remaining dill — taste for seasoning and serve right away.
toolSuggestion: A large pasta pot and a wide skillet

name: Sheet Pan Salmon with Roasted Veggies
pitch: If you have any vegetables hiding in your fridge — even just onion or a potato — this hands-off sheet pan dinner lets the oven do all the work.
steps: Preheat your oven to 400°F (200°C) and line a baking sheet with foil or parchment.
Chop any vegetables you have into similar-sized pieces, toss with oil, salt, and pepper, and spread on the pan — roast for 10 minutes alone first.
Nestle the salmon fillets among the veggies, drizzle with oil, season with salt, pepper, and dill, then lay thin lemon slices on top.
Roast everything together for another 12–15 minutes until the salmon flakes easily, then finish with a squeeze of fresh lemon juice.
